steps.content: The candlelight illuminates the aged study. On the desk at the center of the room lies a note—the handwriting is crooked and messy, but the ink is unmistakably fresh.
<color=#7683a2><i>Don't be afraid. The one outside the door means no harm. You're safe here.</color><i>

Unlike the rest of the castle, this place lacks the suffocating chill and eeriness. Despite being covered in cobwebs and dust, the room somehow radiates a warmth, as if someone has poured their heart into the decor. A soft rustling sound breaks the silence again, and suddenly there's another note beneath the candlestick.
<color=#7683a2><i>Go out and keep right to exit the corridor. No. 15 is waiting for you.</color><i>

The candlestick casts a gentle, warm yellow glow across the cluttered desk and picture frames on the wall. The edges of the frames show signs of decay, and the canvases are covered with a thick layer of dust, making it impossible to discern what they depict.
After wiping away the thick layer of dust, you discover several ancient oil paintings depicting various scenes:

The first painting shows a corridor. Arched vaulted ceilings and carved pillars adorn the hallway, giving it a regal, palace-like grandeur. Sunlight streams through tall stained-glass windows, casting dappled patterns of light, while the stone-tiled floor reflects a subtle sheen. It looks somewhat similar to the corridor outside.

The next painting depicts a magnificent great hall. Enormous crystal chandeliers hang high above, while a long red carpet stretches from the entrance deep into the ceremonial space, adorned throughout with fresh flowers and colorful silk ribbons.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Is this... Morveth Castle from the past?
As if someone heard your question, another note appears on the table.
<color=#7683a2><i>Yes, this place was once a true sanctuary for weddings.</color><i>
Unlike the eerie environment around you, the places in the paintings are colorful, brimming with a sense of vitality and warmth.
The wooden desk where the note sits is cluttered with books, papers, and dried-up ink bottles. You push them aside and uncover a book with a black cover hidden underneath.
The moment your fingers brush against the brittle cover of the book, you hear a sharp, nervous gasp from a shadowy corner of the study.

February 14, N.F. 82, Newlyweds: John Smith & Mary Brown Procurement list: White tulle, rose petals, champagne, cake, candles... February 27, N.F. 82, Newlyweds: James Wilson & Emma Davis Procurement list: Red silk, lilies, red wine, chocolate, music box... March 2, N.F. 82, Newlyweds: Michael Johnson & Lily Martin Procurement list: Blue ribbons, tulips, champagne, fruit tarts, decorative lights...
Flipping through the pages, you can almost feel the castle's former vibrancy, a place once filled with life and joy. Yet, the golden days seem to have been short.

June 28, N.F. 83, Newlyweds: Alexander Green & Sophia Clark Procurement list: White tulle, rose petals, champagne... December 13, N.F. 84, Newlyweds: Henry Taylor & Emily Anderson Procurement list: Red silk, lilies, red wine...
With the DisSea Explosion as a turning point, weddings at the castle steadily declined afterward. Yet, among these records, one entry stands out starkly from the rest.
November 2, N.F. 89, Abandoned infant: unnamed Procurement list: milk powder, diapers, blankets...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: An abandoned infant?

Before you can examine it more closely, a dark shadow flashes before your eyes, snatching the book away. Another scrap of paper has appeared on the desk, the handwriting even more crooked than before:
Don't look!!! (///A///)

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Why can't I look?
Your question is met with silence. But as you glance down, you immediately notice an unmistakable clue.
A familiar white veil peeks out from behind a bookshelf. Adorned with pearls and blue roses, it still bears traces of Mania contamination that hasn't fully faded.

options: Pretend you don't know it's her

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Did you write these notes? Thank you. I hope I'm not disturbing you.

steps.speaker: Very well. You've managed this exceptionally well, after all. You can proceed as you wish.
steps.content: Graves? Weren't you preparing for the wedding? Why are you here?

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: —! I... ahem! I'm not Graves, you've mistaken me for someone else. I'm just a nun who cleans around the castle... That's right, I heard someone was lost, so I came to help. If you follow the corridor to the right, you'll reach the ceremony hall.
Yet another classic case of Graves accidentally giving herself away. It seems her appearance hasn't fully recovered yet, and she doesn't want you to see what she looks like.

options: Right, I've got the wrong person again.
I see, please forgive me for intruding.

steps.content: You choose not to expose her, instead sitting down on the floor with only a row of bookshelves between you. She clearly didn't expect you to get this close—in the flickering candlelight, her silhouette stiffens, curling up tightly as if bracing herself.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Why are you still here?
If you told her you were looking for Graves—and even planned to kick that suspicious shadow in the butt—she'd probably startle like a frightened bird and run off again.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: There aren't any scary monsters in Morveth Castle. They all exist because of lovers' wishes, and they're all my friends.
Your flimsy excuse worked even better than expected—she seems to believe your made-up story. While exploiting her innocence makes you feel a bit guilty, this is definitely a good opportunity.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Thank you for the directions, Sister. You seem quite familiar with Morveth Castle.

options: Then you must know Graves quite well, right?

steps.content: She freezes for a moment, but quickly recovers and slips back into her "role."

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Of course! I'm the nun of the castle after all. I know her better than anyone!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'd like to hear her story.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Why? It's not a good story.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I mean, she is my bride, I've got to learn more about her, right? Marriage takes two people, after all. I can only tell whether a story is good or not after hearing it, and...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I see something in her. I sense that Graves is hiding something from me. I want to learn more about her, and this place.
The figure behind the bookshelf seems to freeze for an instant, but continues speaking nonetheless.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Graves wasn't pretty at all... When Sister Elsie found her, she was just a dark, wrinkled little thing. But Sister Elsie said all babies look like that when they're born.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: But as she grew older, we noticed something was off. Red skin, sharp teeth... she would pounce and bite at the slightest disturbance. She... she wasn't human.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Monster... that's what we all called her.
Her voice grows quieter, and you catch the soft rustle of her burying her face in her arms.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Ever since she arrived, fewer and fewer couples came here to get married. We couldn't make a living anymore, so many of us left one after another. That monster was a bad omen—she brought misfortune to Morveth Castle.

options: She shouldn't be blamed for this.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Couples stopped coming here to get married because of natural disasters and urban development. It wasn't her fault.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: ...It was her fault. If she'd done as she was told and stayed hidden, she wouldn't have scared off so many couples. Morveth Castle wouldn't have been left with nothing but those awful ghost wedding stories.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: She tried to hide her face, but ruining things was always what she did best... You know, ever since she was little, she loved hiding in the corners of the hall to secretly watch the wedding ceremonies. Sister Elsie caught her several times.

options: I've heard Graves mention her before.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She's no longer here with us, is she?

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Sister Elsie was very old, even older than the Morveth Castle itself. She said she would eventually have to leave... She said all human stories follow the same pattern—people meet, then part ways.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: So she was alone again. She stuck to her usual routine: waking up, praying, making lunch, and then hiding where no one could see her, waiting for couples to arrive. It went on like that for a very, very long time, until everyone forgot Morveth Castle even existed.
Graves's voice becomes muffled and subdued. She clearly doesn't like telling this story.
You're separated by bookshelves, unable to see each other's expressions. Candlelight flickers between the wooden shelves, bathing you in a gentle warm glow while leaving Graves hidden in shadow.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So Graves has always felt abandoned. What she wants isn't just a ceremony, is it?
You lean closer toward her side of the bookshelf, the aged wood creaking softly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What she really wants is...

options: A fate where she's never abandoned.

steps.content: You can't see her face, but through the gaps between the books, you glimpse the veil-wearing girl clutching her arms tightly as she lifts her head.

Above your heads, the bookshelves display the past of this wedding sanctuary: books on wedding cultures from Outlands and photo albums of newlywed couples captured in moments of blessing. To her, they are like stars in the night sky, offering solace when her insecurities and doubts creep in.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But these only show you the most beautiful moments in relationships. I'm no expert on this subject myself—since I got questioned about it in the hallway. But... are "weddings" and what you truly want really the same thing?
Graves begins to tremble defensively, as though her most guarded secret has been laid bare. That familiar dark shadow once again weaves itself around her form.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: It will happen, I know it will. As long as I stay beautiful and attentive, I'll eventually find someone who won't abandon me.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: ...For better, for worse, for richer, for poorer, in sickness and in health, in joy and in sadness, to support and cherish me...
She speaks faster and faster, her voice shaking violently.

steps.speaker: Graves?
steps.content: I've waited for so long. Why haven't things worked out? It's because I don't deserve it, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Graves?
steps.content: No one wants to stay with me! Everyone always abandons me!

This is it—the source of the obsession feeding the Mania crisis at Morveth Castle: Graves's hidden side. Her suppressed emotions break free from their disguise, twisting and writhing as they take shape, threatening to swallow her whole.
This unusual Mania doesn't stem from an external force—it is born from the insecurity, loneliness, suffering, and confusion that have always resided within her.
Without hesitation, you rise to your feet and move behind the bookshelf, approaching her desperate figure as she digs her claws into her skin in despair. Gently, you take hold of her decaying hands.
